Subject: SLO measurement & access Qs for procurement packet

Hi Priya / Redwood team,

Thanks for the RFP response — procurement asks are focused on how you measure and expose uptime/latency commitments. Our security and platform teams want clear, reproducible answers we can include in the contract. Specifically:
- How are SLOs defined and calculated (rolling window, error budget calculation)?
- What telemetry do you capture (ingest points, sampling rates, retention)?
- What alerting thresholds and escalation paths exist for latency and availability incidents?
- Can customers get read-only access to telemetry dashboards or raw metric exports, and if so, under what constraints?

Can you send a short packet we can attach to the procurement file and a pointer to any dashboards or sample exports we can review? We are aiming to finalize the procurement checklist by end of next week.

Best,
Peter Liu
Head of Platform Engineering
Orion Health

Attachment: procurement-slo-questions.xlsx (referenced)

From: priya_natarajan@redwood.ai

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SLO measurement & access Qs for procurement packet

Peter — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a concise playbook that answers each point and included a short instrumentation sample you can hand to your SREs. High level summary below; the full packet (PDF) is attached.

Summary answers:
- Definition & calculation: Redwood defines availability SLOs on a per-route per-model basis (successful 2xx token generation within configured latency threshold). The rolling window is 30 days by default, with an optional 7-day fast window for rapid regressions. Error budget = 1 - availability for the window; we compute both request-weighted and token-weighted budgets depending on contract.
- Telemetry captured: request/response latency histograms (p50/p90/p99), request success/failure counters, model-variant KPIs (quantization/seq_len buckets), sampling of raw request IDs for replay (1% default, configurable), and KV-cache hit rates. Metric retention: 90 days for full resolution, 13 months for aggregated daily rollups.
- Alerting & escalation: threshold-based alerts on p99 and error-rate windows (1m/5m/30m) plus automated on-call paging. We provide runbooks and a postmortem cadence; critical incidents trigger a tactical incident channel with SLA owner escalation.
- Customer telemetry access: we offer time-limited read-only dashboard invites (Grafana) and a metric export API (CSV, up to 30 days per request). For customers requiring raw traces, we support limited trace exports under NDA and audit review.

Attachments included: redwood_slo_measurement_playbook_v1.pdf, instrumentation-sample-cmds.txt, readme-dashboard-invite.txt

Next steps: if Orion wants a temporary read-only Grafana invite or a 48-hour sample export of metrics for a specific route, we can provision that today. Otherwise we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough for your SREs.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

--

Peter — adding some technical specifics you can pass to your SREs: 

Instrumentation & sampling notes (technical):
- Client-facing metrics are emitted at the edge before tokenization and after model response so the latency window includes network + runtime.
- Latency histogram buckets: [0-50ms, 50-100ms, 100-200ms, 200-500ms, 500-1000ms, 1s+]; we export p50/p90/p95/p99.
- Sampling: default 1% of requests captured with full payload for replay; customers can opt-in for higher sampling rates for specific routes for a temporary window (requires acceptance of privacy terms).
- KV-cache and cold-start detection: we tag metrics with cache_hit=true/false and maintain short-lived per-model cold-start counters to help correlate p99 spikes.
- Replay artifacts: instrumentation-sample-cmds.txt contains curl examples for requesting a metric export and for requesting a replay bundle.

If you want a quick sandbox demo, we can spin up a small sample route and send a 6-hour metrics export tied to your test tenant. That export is safe to share internally at Orion after we scrub PII.

— Karthik
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Peter — quick operational note on access patterns:
- For procurement, we typically grant a 14-day read-only Grafana invite scoped to the account and specific routes; this is sufficient for most auditors to validate dashboarded SLOs.
- For exceptions (e.g., if your compliance team wants longer-term access), we can create a time-limited service account with exported CSV access for up to 90 days subject to an export request ticket and an NDA addendum.
- Any dashboard invites are read-only, enforce IP allowlists if requested, and audit logs are delivered as part of the evidence packet.

If Orion wants the 14-day invite, tell us which email addresses to add and whether you need IP restrictions. We will also include a short video walkthrough and a link to the SLO playbook.

Grace O'Connor
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
